newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mixed ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mixed ahead of report.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ranged mixed at the close as evening up ahead of USDA's Cattle-on-Feed report dominated the market, traders said.
Trading activity was light much of the session as many traders kept to the sidelines ahead of the government data and part of early gains were erased in late balancing action.

Early support reflected expectations of firmer fed cattle markets next week, unless there is a bearish slant to the cattle report, traders said. But spread action weighed on December late while supporting February and April, they noted.

Boxed beef values declined this week but beef sales have been fairly active and packers should need to replenish slaughter numbers. Near-term fed cattle supplies appear tight which kept October futures firm, sources said.

Estimates for October 1 on-feed cattle supplies at major feedlots in Friday's monthly report averaged 94.8 percent of a year ago and ranged from 93.8 to 97. However, September placement estimates averaged 98.6 in a range of 96.2 to 104 percent and compare with large placements last year. Marketing estimates averaged 87.8 and ranged from 85 to 90.8 percent of a year ago.
In live cattle options, there was bear spreading, buying of December 65 puts and selling of 62 puts early. There was also demand for February 68 calls, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures closed higher on declining feed prices and a higher CME feeder cattle index, traders said. Support from early gains in the neighboring live cattle pit also bolstered values initially.
The latest CME index was up $0.35 at $63.16 per cwt.
E.D.& F. Man and LIT division of First Options spread long November/short October, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.525 cents a lb higher to 0.050 lower with December off 0.050 at 65.350 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.075 to 0.400 with November up most at 64.075 cents.
